set_aside.subject: Python dependency digest
set_aside.question: What concrete artifact is the digest for the Python version required to identify: the source distribution, the installed interpreter executable, a CPython installation package, or another complete runtime artifact?
options: Digest the package or archive from which the complete CPython runtime is installed.
set_aside.default_guess: Digest the immutable package or archive that supplies the complete CPython runtime.

witness.initial: Two installations report the same exact CPython version, but one was built with modified patches and different binaries.
events: The release author records the official CPython source digest and the exact version.
The installer receives the modified build whose source-version label and recorded source digest match, but whose runtime binaries differ.
outcomes: The installation succeeds because the digest identifies the source release.
The installation fails because the digest must identify the runtime artifact actually installed.
witness.observer: The release installer and the owner see whether the modified runtime is admitted.

set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: dependency inventory boundary
set_aside.text: After an installation that succeeded, the dependencies the running instance has are exactly the release's list, by name, version and digest, nothing more.
set_aside.question: Are system libraries and the store engine separate dependencies that must each appear by name, version and digest, or are they represented solely by the base-image entry whose digest fixes them?
options: List every system library and the store engine separately.
Treat the base image as the single listed dependency representing all system libraries and the store engine.
List only libraries dynamically loaded by Registry, while representing all other image contents by the base-image digest.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the base-image digest as the inventory of its system libraries and store engine, while listing Python packages and Python separately.

witness.initial: A base image contains CPython, the store engine, libc, OpenSSL and other system libraries; the release list contains the base image, Python and every Python package, but no separate entries for libc, OpenSSL or the store engine.
events: The release process validates the list against rule 1.
The installation attempts to start Registry from that image.
outcomes: The release is made because the base-image digest fixes the unlisted system components.
The release is refused because the running instance has dependencies that are not separately present in the list.
witness.observer: The release author sees whether the same release manifest is accepted.

set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: Linux base image qualification
set_aside.text: A release whose base image is not a Linux one
set_aside.question: What observable property makes a base image “a Linux one”?
options: Its image manifest declares the Linux operating-system platform.
It is built from a recognized Linux distribution and records that distribution.
Its contained executables and libraries target the Linux ABI, including a scratch or distroless image.
set_aside.default_guess: Require Linux platform metadata and Linux-ABI contents; do not require a named distribution.

witness.initial: A distroless image declares an OCI Linux platform and contains Linux CPython and its libraries, but has no distribution name or release file.
events: The release process applies Required test 5 to the image.
The release author requests that the image be admitted.
outcomes: The image passes because its declared platform and ABI are Linux.
The image fails because no recognized Linux distribution identifies it as a Linux base image.
witness.observer: The release author sees whether the release is made.

set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: digest form in the release manifest
set_aside.text: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest
set_aside.question: Which digest algorithm, textual representation and artifact-identity fields does the release format use for each dependency kind?
options: Use a fixed SHA-256 digest with a canonical algorithm-prefixed encoding.
Use the native digest identifier supplied by each package or image ecosystem.
Use an algorithm-tagged digest field that permits an approved set of algorithms.
consequences: A single fixed form makes comparison simple but requires every input ecosystem to be normalized.
Native forms reduce conversion but make validation and equality rules dependency-kind-specific.
An algorithm-tagged form supports migration but requires generation to define the allowed algorithms and canonical comparison.
set_aside.requirement: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest
set_aside.default_guess: Use a canonical algorithm-tagged SHA-256 digest over the immutable installation artifact.

set_aside.subject: non-Linux host installation check
set_aside.text: Installing a release on a host whose kernel is not Linux's fails, and no instance of it starts (rule 6).
set_aside.question: How does installation establish the host kernel identity before any Registry instance starts?
options: Read the running kernel identity locally and fail closed before process creation.
Require trusted deployment attestation of the host kernel and validate it before process creation.
Combine trusted platform metadata with a local kernel-identity check and require both to agree.
consequences: A local check is simple but depends on the installer's view not being virtualized or spoofed.
Attestation can bind the physical or virtual host more strongly but adds deployment infrastructure and credential handling.
Requiring both is stricter and detects disagreement, but rejects installations where attestation is unavailable.
set_aside.requirement: Installing a release on a host whose kernel is not Linux's fails, and no instance of it starts (rule 6).
set_aside.default_guess: Check the running kernel locally before starting Registry and fail closed; use attestation when the deployment environment already supplies it.

witness.initial: An installation target presents Linux-compatible userland and image metadata, while the underlying host kernel is not Linux; Registry has not started.
events: The deployer validates the target before process creation.
One deployment implementation trusts image and platform metadata; another verifies or attests the running host kernel.
outcomes: The metadata-only installation proceeds and starts Registry.
The kernel-verifying installation fails and starts no instance.
witness.observer: The deployer sees whether installation is refused, and callers see whether Registry starts.
